messages.subject: mc-stan.org web pages up
parts:
I created the web pages for Stan and put them
up at:

http://mc-stan.org/

(mcstan.org and mc-stan.com redirect here, too.)

Let me know if you have comments or suggestions (I'm
guessing it will look awful on non-retina Macs).

The source is checked into Git under:

stan/web/*

I tried to keep things as minimal as Andrew wanted
on the home page (and other pages). I also think it's
a good idea -- just a lot of work.

The most extreme form of this is that there are no nav bars,
only a link at the bottom of each page pointing back to the
home page. (This could be a breadcrumb arrangement if we
introduce hieararchical structure.)

I couldn't figure out how to incorporate the logo
graphically in this minimal setup.

To keep the user-experience coherent for our visitors,
and to get as much search engine juice as possible, we
should move all of our text to mc-stan.org, including:

-- R Getting Started wiki
-- C++ API doc

That means rewriting the Wiki in HTML, which I'm
happy to do.

Google Code will continue to host

-- Git repository
-- source distribution: stan-version.tgz
-- doc distribution: stan-reference.pdf

and Google Groups will continue to host

-- mailing lists

We should also simplify

-- google code home page
-- API doc home page

both of which are out of date and redundant.

I tried to set up forwarding from

st...@mc-stan.org

to mc.sta...@gmail.com, which in turn forwards
to me and Daniel. If you'd also like to be a recipient,
let us know or configure it yourself by logging in
as mc.stanislaw. It doesn't work yet, though the
interface indicates it's configured to do the right thing.
Maybe tomorrow...

I can hand out web login info for mc-stan.org
at our next meeting or via e-mail.

I still need to write the C++ and command-line
quick start guides (and the full C++ guide, too).

- Bob

parts:
Michael -- that looks much more professional
than the bare-bones layout I did.

Andrew was pretty adamant about moving from
Google Code to a minimal home page with only
a handful of links. Specifically the ones in
the outline he sent. I edited those a bit,
which is where mc-stan.org is at now.

So the big question is:

header + multi-column layout or not?

I haven't heard from Andrew for a few days, so maybe
we can resolve this when he gets back.

Until then, I'm going to leave what's already up there
up and wait until we decide on a basic philosophy
before looking into the layouts in detail.

Anyone else care about what the web pages look like?
If so, now would be a good time to speak up!

- Bob
